title: Taming implies compatibility
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: An exposition of OpenAI's proof (2026) that on a closed four-manifold every almost complex structure tamed by a symplectic form admits a compatible symplectic form, answering Donaldson's tamed-to-compatible question. The proof is given in full from one named hypothesis, (HK): the Hodge Laplacian on two-forms is the Levi-Civita connection Laplacian plus an endomorphism, and its heat kernel has the strong short-time asymptotics and the Gaussian upper bound proved by Ludewig. The first lesson sets up the pointwise algebra of two-forms, a closed lift of anti-invariant forms through a projected elliptic operator, the measure representation of positive functionals on invariant forms, and the separating current. The second proves quadratic mass growth of its trace measure with radial test forms. The third regularizes with (1 + r^2 Delta)^-3 and proves that the correction is square integrable and that nearby complex lines of the current align. The fourth proves that the density exists everywhere and that tangent measures at points of positive density are planar. The fifth proves that the positive-density part of the current is closed, removes the correction by a final pairing, and reaches a contradiction with the taming form.
prerequisites: course Elliptic boundary reduction, lessons Symbols, finite defects, and the index on a closed manifold; Detecting regularity without choosing coordinates; Symbols, operators and Sobolev scales: bundle Sobolev spaces, the elliptic alternative, operators of order zero and their composition

checks.reading: The manuscript 'Taming implies compatibility on four-manifolds' (OpenAI, 23 Sep 2026; main.tex, preamble.tex, references.bib and seven section files, 1,487 lines of TeX) was read in full on 14 Oct 2026, and every step of its argument was derived again while the lessons were written: the pointwise algebra of invariant and anti-invariant forms; the symbol of R d d^* on anti-invariant forms; the generalized inverse and the closed lift; separation and the order-zero bound; the measure representation; the correction Q and its Sobolev class; the radial test forms, their Hessian traces, the first-order property of R dd^c and the dyadic estimate of the correction; the zero pairing; the gamma-integral formula for (1 + r^2 Delta)^-6 and the decomposition of its kernel; the angular identity; the positive pairing; the mixing lemma; the energy inequality, Q in L^2 and the angular bound; the vanishing cross terms; the almost monotone density with the C^{1,1} radial functions; the Lebesgue-point estimate; vague limits, closed constant currents, rank two and planar tangent measures; the transverse moment; the density cutoffs and their derivatives; theta = 0 almost everywhere; the L^2 correction error; the tangential estimate with the product of angular and transverse errors; the weights b(f_r) and b_n; the final pairing. No error found. Differences of presentation, none a correction: the measure representation is constructed explicitly through Hermitian 2 x 2 matrices and a Borel choice of measures with given barycentre, in place of a measurable spectral decomposition; the generalized inverse comes from the programme's elliptic alternative (the inverse of L + H); the off-diagonal kernel bound for operators of order zero and the estimate on concentrated inputs are proved in the second lesson; currents are regularized on the scale H^-4 -> H^2 with an interpolation inequality for odd orders; at points of positive density the complex line of the current is identified with the polarization through the identity integral of |l - A|^2 = integral of (1 - |A|^2), without conditional measures; theta = 0 volume-almost everywhere is derived from the Besicovitch covering theorem. The hypothesis (HK) was matched to its free sources on 14 Oct 2026: Ludewig, arXiv:1607.05152v3, Theorem 1.1 (strong asymptotics) and Theorem 3.5 (Gaussian upper bound), and arXiv:1607.05891v3, Section 3, (3.4) (the leading coefficient). Donaldson's question was read in arXiv:math/0607083v1, Section 5.2, Question 2. Programme results used were looked up in the programme's lessons and their statements read: Symbols, finite defects, and the index on a closed manifold ((I1), (I2), (I4)-(I7), Section 3 with (I9)); Detecting regularity without choosing coordinates (Sections 4, 5 and 13, (G32)); Symbols, operators and Sobolev scales ((E10), (E12)); Geodesics, normal coordinates and curvature (Theorem B.1); Riemannian connections and convex neighbourhoods (Theorems B.3, B.5); Jacobi fields, conjugate points and the Morse index theorem (Theorems A.1, A.3, B.2); Order, positivity and distributional limits (Lemma 3.1, Corollary 3.3, Theorem 4.1); Besicovitch's covering theorem and the differentiation of Radon measures (Theorems 4.1, 5.1); Hahn-Banach, Baire and the basic theorems on Banach spaces (Theorem 6.2); Hilbert spaces and compact operators (Theorems 2.3, 6.2); Weak topologies (Theorem 3.1, Proposition 3.2, Exercise 4). Their proofs were not checked again. Checked by the program plan/checks_20261014/tc_check.py (seven parts: the pointwise algebra in random unitary frames; the Hermitian description and the spectral formula of the barycentres; the symbol of R d d^* and its polarization; the angular identity for random complex structures and rotations; the radial Hessian traces with exact Hessians; the gamma integral, the suprema of lambda^j (1 + r^2 lambda)^-3 and the Gaussian domination inequality; the radial functions phi_a, the semipositivity of dd^c log t and its vanishing on complex lines, the centred-ball integrand, the constant c_h and the dyadic sums). open_obligations: Named hypothesis (HK): the Hodge Laplacian on two-forms of a closed Riemannian four-manifold is the Levi-Civita connection Laplacian plus a curvature endomorphism (Weitzenboeck formula), and its heat kernel satisfies the leading-term short-time asymptotics with remainder C t^-1 e^{-c_0 d^2/t} + C_M t^M near the diagonal and the Gaussian upper bound (Ludewig, arXiv:1607.05152, Theorems 1.1 and 3.5; arXiv:1607.05891, Section 3). Not proved in the programme; it enters only through Lemma 3.1 of the third lesson.
The programme results on elliptic operators, Riemannian geometry, measures and functional analysis that are used are cited with their numbers; their proofs were not checked again for this course.

The context results quoted in the first lesson (earlier special cases of the question; Donaldson's remark on higher dimensions) are not used and were not checked; Corollary 1.2 of the manuscript (the cone identity, from Li and Zhang's cone comparison) is not treated.
The lessons were written and checked by one model in one session; they have not been checked by a second reader.
